COLIGNY: A TOWN ON THE EDGE

By: Nicky Troll | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Coligny a town on the edge - violence errupts following the death of teenager at the hands of two farmers.

Unique Selling Point:
NEWS STORY FOR THE WEEK - BEEN BUILDING UP SINCE LAST WEEK - RELEVANT BIGGER PICTURE

Further information:
Pieter Doorewaard and Phillip Schutte are accused of killing Matlhomola Jonas Mosweu, 16, of the Scotland informal settlement in Coligny on April 20.

The two allegedly caught Mosweu, generally known as Faki, stealing sunflowers in their field near the informal settlement.

They reportedly put him at the back of a van with the intention of taking him to the Coligny police station.

However, he allegedly jumped out of the moving van when it reduced speed and suffered neck injuries and later died on his way to hospital.

The men allege that after the teenager jumped from off the van, they went to the police station about 3 kilometres away to report the incident and ask the police to call an ambulance.

However, an eyewitness told police the pair had allegedly pushed or thrown Faki out of the moving van.

The Coligny Magistrate’s Court is expected to rule on the bail application on Monday. The men indicted in their affidavits that they could afford bail of R20,000.

The South African Civic Organisation (Sanco) in the North West plans to march to the court on Monday in an attempt to persuade the court not to grant the pair bail. Sanco North West secretary Packet Seaketso said the march was also to protest against racism in Coligny. He called on white people who opposed racism to join the march.

South African Democratic Teachers’ Union (Sadtu) provincial chairperson, Mxolisi Bomvana, said the time had come for whites who opposed racism to take action. “They must be seen marching with us against racism. To donate cows or money in silence is not enough, they must take action,” he told mourners at Mosweu’s funeral service on Sunday.


THEMES
- WHAT HAPPENED IS UNCLEAR...
- IS THIS COLIGNY SCENARIO A REPRESENTATION OF A GREATER SOUTH AFRICA?
- WHAT IMPACT WILL IT HAVE ON THE TOWN FROM AN ECONOMIC POINT OF VIEW?
- WILL THERE BE JUSTICE?
- CONCERN ABOUT VIOLENCE AND CIVIL JUSTICE IF THERE IS A SENSE THAT THE JUSTICE SYSTEM WILL NOT DELIVER A FAIR JUDGEMENT?
- COULD THE VIOLENCE BE A BUILD UP OF BIGGER UNDERLYING ISSUES AND RACIAL INJUSTICES?
- HOW DO WE FIX SOUTH AFRICA? HOW DO WE MOVE FORWARD?
-

SANCO - PACKET SEAKETSO / REPRESENTATIVE STRUCTURE IN COLIGNY - VOICE FOR BLACK COMMUNITY
FARMING REPRESENTATIVE - VOICE FOR WHITE COMMUNITY

SAYS THE PROTEST IS ALSO FUELLED BY A LOT OF UNDERLYING FACTORS - LIKE UNEMPLOYMENT, AN INEFFECTIVE JUSTICE SYSTEM...

Press Release:


Coligny
As South Africa continues to grapple with racial tension, this week Coligny in the North West became the focal point. Two farmers accused of the murder of a teenage boy
allegedly over the theft of sunflowers, were granted bail. Some residents believe the killing was racially motivated. As tempers flared, a number of houses were burnt and
property damaged by community members protesting their release. Carte Blanche analyses this developing story

Script:


COLIGNY STRUCTURE

VO: The racial unrest spotlight has been cast on the small maize and sunflower farming town of Coligny in the North West Province.

It all started with an alleged criminal act that resulted in the death of a 16 year old boy on the 20th of April.

Matlhomola Mosweu was accused of stealing sunflowers and apprehended by two farm employees, who claim they were taking him to the police station. But, he didn’t make it there.

LINK: Was he beaten, did he jump off the back of a bakkie, was he pushed – we don’t know. But what we do know is that, that tragic event was the tipping point for the community.

STANNY: It changed everything, it changed the province – his death triggered something in South Africa.

VO: Three days after Matlhomola’s death – no arrests had been made. School teacher Stanny Mnyakama is his family’s spokesperson.

STANNY: The family was devastated they couldn’t take it, the father was saying to us – you this boy, I was expecting a lot form his son – but now he’s dead – turn Coligny to a ghost town

VO: Fuelled by their frustration, the community took the streets of Coligny - leaving behind a trial of destruction.

Businesses along the main road were damaged, shops in town and the surrounding townships were looted and trucks burnt beyond repair.

COBUS: Dunno how to explain myself, but I cried for a few seconds – three trucks out of 12, out of your income

LINK: Most of the shops are not directly linked to the case – in fact the majority of the stores are owned by foreign nationals – three weeks later, the destruction is still visible.

ISLAM: We are broken, the heart is broken. // we don’t know nothing about it – they came and broke our shops, they make it empty – there is nothing left inside

VO: Islam Mainul represents a group of Bangladeshi shop owners – together they ran over 20 shops in and around Coligny – collectively they’ve lost close to R3 million worth of stock.

Their homes were also looted and the group is now staying at the local mosque.

ISLAM: We are afraid, we are afraid to stay…

VO: Following the riots, Pieter Doorewaard and Phillip Schutte were arrested and charged with the murder of Matlhomola Mosweu on the 24th April. But that would not be the end of the unrest in Coligny – the bail hearing would bring a fresh wave violence.

UPSOUND FATHER: My son is gone, what about his life. This can’t be.

BRIG: They were then were granted R5000 bail each – unfortunately that particular incident also lead to the destruction of properties.

VO: Brigadier Sabata Mokgwabone confirmed that the houses of three residents - not linked to the criminal case - were set alight by community members.

STANNY: When people are furious you can’t control them - they hit at anyone associated with white.

BRIG: It was apparent that there were some criminal elements – when we were trying to explain to the community what transpired we could see there some were hell bent on committing crime.

VO: While the situation was tense – business owner Cobus van Tonder says retaliation was not an option.

COBUS: Fighting back was never on our minds that’s why kept everyone quiet … and see that everyone is safe INT2 M15

VO: They even went as far as to block people from historically right wing neighbouring towns from coming into Coligny.

COBUS: Ons het so gese – GEEN KONFRONTASIE – nothing! We were there to be the eyes for the police.

VO: Currently there is still a strong police presence in the town, with cops patrolling the streets and a chopper monitoring the area.

Packet Seaketso is from the South African National Civic Organisation – he says while they condemn violent and criminal conduct - racism must fall.

PACKET: Coligny has serious racial tension amongst the black and white I would say.

VO: But while residents say there is a clear division, Mnkayama acknowledges that not everyone is the same.

STANNY: Some whites are not good. Not all white people are racists, I got examples

VO: It became evident at Matlhomola’s funeral, that racism would be used as a theme by politicians when Premier Supra Mahumapelo took to the floor.

UPSOUND North West premier Supra Mahumapelo:
What happened is that he lost his life when he was in the hands of some white people who are racist.

KERWIN: The things is, our leadership at the moment has been using a race a lot lately to polarise people, when they should be trying to unify the country…

VO: Kerwin Lebone from the Institute of Race Relations says this a very dangerous game.

DEVI: The conclusion is that it’s racism…
KERWIN: We can never have definitive conclusion on something we know nothing about – the court is going to deal with criminality – the problem with south African we are very quick to ascribe racism as a motive.

VO: While the judicial process must run its course, we should not underestimate the undertones of racism, says Former Gauteng Judge President, Judge Bernard Ngoepe.

JUDGE: When people begin to jump to certain conclusion – to say there was racism involved – it is because they dig into experience, unfortunate experience.

VO: Boeta du Toit represents the farming community in the North West – he believes what’s happening in Coligny goes beyond race.

BOETA: If you go look if it goes about racism – you must go look who’s home have been burnt down and business, there was not distinction made between different races – it was lawlessness – and what we see here is a manifestation of a country that is falling to pieces, as a result of the political and economic decline.

DEVI: Why do you think you were targeted?
ISLAM: Really also we don’t know if those 2 young white guys was doing shit, they should go to them – not to us.

LINK: But nothing exist in a vacuum – together with underlying racial tensions, there has been a spate of service delivery protests in this province too – the area is economically depressed – and the majority of people access to basic services.

PACKET: There is generally poor service delivery – not only in the NW but in the country – //some of the protests are genuinely – some are man made if you drive in the township of Coligny – there is sewer flowing all over the township…

VO: No matter the motivation - this kind of criminality will not be tolerated says Brigadeir Mokgwabone.

BRIG: We need to be careful of as South Africans – we need to control our emotions // WE are not going to condone crime we will make sure that those that commit crime are arrested.

DEVI: How do we fix this?
JUDGE: I wish I knew, but what I do know is we can’t just do nothing // the judicial system, the policing system, must also play their part to make sure that people do have and retain confidence which will address the problems so that they stand back and give the system some chance.

PROMOS
PROMO 1
VO: Racial tension flared up in the North West after the alleged murder of a 16 year old boy.

STANNY: It changed everything, it changed the province – his death triggered something in South Africa.

PROMO 2
VO: The Coligny community left a trial of destruction protesting the release of two men charged with the murder of a young boy.

STANNY: When people are furious you can’t control them - they hit at anyone associated with white.

PROMO 3
VO: The town of Coligny was looted after the death of teenager at the hands of two farm employees.

ISLAM: Tihey came and broke our shops, they make it empty – there is nothing left inside
